extracted.intended_audience: mathematics communicators, exhibition organizers, outreach coordinators, and editors involved with IMAGINARY or similar math-communication projects
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and documented standards for organizing IMAGINARY mathematics exhibitions, running SURFER competitions/workshops, operating the IMAGINARY network, and producing the 'Snapshots of modern mathematics from Oberwolfach' publications. Covers content components, technical infrastructure, editorial processes, and outreach/metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accessibility and online documentation of events
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2015, IMAGINARY organized 56 exhibition events which are easily accessible for everyone through the database on the website. Usually, events will have a short description but also other media such as photographs, or even videos summarizing each event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All events should be listed in the online database, include a short descriptive text and supporting media (photos, videos) so they are easily accessible to the public and documented for reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of interactive touch-screen stations
rubrics_metrics.description: MPE exhibition components included multiple touch screen stations (e.g., six in Heidelberg, four in London).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide interactive touchscreen software stations as part of exhibitions to engage visitors; use open-source IMAGINARY/MPE software where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of hands-on experiment stations
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibitions featured several hands-on experimentierstationen (e.g., eight hands-on stations in Heidelberg and London).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include hands-on, tactile stations that allow direct experimentation to increase visitor engagement, particularly for younger audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical image galleries and large-format prints
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibitions included a gallery of mathematical images and large-format images (e.g., 22 big-format images in Slovenia; 35 gallery prints in Belgium).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curate high-quality mathematical imagery and consider large-format prints for public and outdoor displays; provide image galleries both in-person and online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Film/animation stations and screenings
rubrics_metrics.description: Some exhibitions presented film stations and screened animations (e.g., a film station in London; 'Katzengold' animation screened at Bridges Short Movie Festival).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a film/animation station to present mathematical animations and videos; use screenings and festival submissions to broaden outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3D-printed and sculptural mathematical objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibitions showcased 3D-prints of mathematical objects and sculptures (e.g., 12 3D-prints in Belgium; 3D sculptures in Taiwan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce and display tangible 3D models to illustrate mathematical forms; include locally-produced content where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration with local museums and research institutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibitions were organized in collaboration with local partners (e.g., Heidelberg Laureate Forum Foundation, HITS, Museum für Mineralien und Mathematik (MiMa), EPSRC Centre at Imperial College).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partner with local museums, institutes, and academic centers to source exhibits, share infrastructure, and increase visibility and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traveling exhibitions and local adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: IMAGINARY initiated traveling (Wanderausstellungen) exhibitions in multiple countries and presented IMAGINARY for the first time in several new countries. Local versions included newly devised and produced content (e.g., Uruguay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design exhibitions to be transportable and adaptable; encourage local partners to produce region-specific content to increase relevance and ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshops targeted at young mathematicians and visitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Several projects combined exhibitions with workshops, mainly for young mathematicians (e.g., two workshops in Israel; weekend workshops in Taiwan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include workshops alongside exhibitions to engage students and early-career mathematicians; tailor content (hands-on, SURFER sessions) to audience age and experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent installation possibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An exhibition was permanently installed at the Nesin Mathematics Village in Turkey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where feasible, plan for permanent or semi-permanent installations to provide long-term public engagement and continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of SURFER software for competitions and creative workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: SURFER competitions and SURFER workshops were held in multiple countries; participants created images with SURFER. IMAGINARY provided the database and online gallery and participated in evaluation committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run software-based art competitions/workshops (SURFER) to involve broad communities, use centralized database/gallery for submissions, and form evaluation committees to judge entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of technical infrastructure (IMAGINARY-Live-Linux, dynamic museum system)
rubrics_metrics.description: An IMAGINARY-Live-Linux system was developed to simplify installation and distribution of IMAGINARY programs; infrastructure is based on a dynamic museum system and will include monitoring and power-management tools (for ESO Supernova museum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide ready-to-use technical stacks (live Linux images, packaged exhibit software) and management/monitoring tools to ease deployment for local partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network infrastructure and services (database, interactive map, newsletter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The new math communication network created a database and an interactive map of worldwide math museums with background information; a bi-monthly network newsletter is published; a community-maintained database of activities is planned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain centralized, discoverable resources (databases, maps) and regular communications (newsletter); plan for community curation and shared idea-collections to foster exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: MaTiE translations initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics Translations in Europe (MaTiE) works on establishing a media network to translate selected popular mathematics articles into European languages and share them among partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate cross-language dissemination by translating curated popular-math articles and sharing them via the network to broaden reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Snapshots: topical selection connected to MFO workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Snapshots selected by organizers describe a scientific topic in connection with a workshop at the MFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose snapshot topics that link directly to current workshop/research themes to leverage expert participation and topical relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Snapshots: length and languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Snapshots are ca. 8–12 DIN A5 pages long and are written in German or English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constrain snapshot length to 8–12 A5 pages and accept English or German to maintain consistency and readability for target audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Snapshots: editorial process and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The director of the MFO addresses workshop organizers about snapshots. The project is coordinated by Dr. Carla Cederbaum, who acts as chief editor; junior editors edited snapshots in 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement a clear editorial workflow with a coordinator/chief editor communicating with workshop organizers and a team of editors to prepare and vet content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Snapshots: target audience and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Target readership consists of mathematics teachers, science journalists, undergraduates, advanced high school students, and the interested public. The project aims to promote understanding of and appreciation for modern mathematics and mathematical research worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write snapshots to be accessible to teachers, journalists, students, and interested lay readers; focus on clarity and fostering appreciation rather than heavy technical detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication channels for snapshots
rubrics_metrics.description: Snapshots were published both on the IMAGINARY platform and on the MFO website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish snapshots on multiple platforms (project site and institutional site) to maximize dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of visitor metrics as evidence of impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Visitor numbers are cited (e.g., ~27,000 visitors in Weizmann exhibition; >10,000 in Uruguay; >1,000 participants in Senegal) as indicators of reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track and report visitor/participant counts for exhibitions and events as part of impact assessment and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of locally contributed interdisciplinary works
rubrics_metrics.description: Local experts contributed works combining mathematics and art (e.g., Taiwan contributions), and Uruguay produced entirely local content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage and integrate local interdisciplinary contributions (math+art) to increase cultural relevance and diversify exhibit content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in conferences and outreach festivals
rubrics_metrics.description: IMAGINARY activities included presentations at conferences (e.g., Bridges) and participation in festivals (e.g., Glasgow Science Festival, Berlin Science Night).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage established conferences and science-festival events to showcase exhibits, run workshops, and reach broader interdisciplinary audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support from funding and institutional programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects were funded or supported by organizations (e.g., Cap’Maths, BMBF 'Research in Germany' campaign, UNESCO, German Embassy/DWIH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek institutional and funding support to enable international exhibitions, translations, and outreach activities; acknowledge partners and funders in documentation.
